types.embedding_query_text: Actor: A person who performs in films, television, or theater. Also called performer, thespian, movie star. Examples: Ryan Gosling, Nicolas Cage, Eva Mendes, Gosling.

chosen_type.label: PerformanceRole
chosen_type.justification: Actors like Ryan Gosling, Nicolas Cage, and Eva Mendes play roles in performances, fitting PerformanceRole.

candidates.label: PerformanceRole
candidates.comment: A PerformanceRole, as a Role, is a role an entity plays in a theatrical performance, such as a movie or TV series. Also called acting role, character role, stage role. Examples: 'actor in a film', 'director of a play', 'musician in a concert'. Distinct from OrganizationRole, which is a role within an organization.

candidates.label: PerformingArtsTheater
candidates.comment: A PerformingArtsTheater is a civic structure or venue for performing arts. Also called theater, playhouse, concert hall. Examples: Sydney Opera House, a local community theater, a Broadway theater. Distinct from MovieTheater, which is for film screenings.

candidates.label: PerformingArtsEvent
candidates.comment: A PerformingArtsEvent is an event featuring live performances of arts like music, theatre, dance, or acrobatics. Also called live performance, show, stage event. Examples: a Broadway play, a ballet performance, a circus show, a stand-up comedy act. Distinct from MusicEvent, which is specifically for music.

candidates.label: TheaterEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing a live performance in a theater. Also called stage play, theatrical show, drama performance. Examples: a Broadway musical, a local community play, a Shakespearean tragedy.

candidates.label: MovieTheater
candidates.comment: A MovieTheater is a civic structure designed for public viewing of movies. Also called cinema, picture house, movie house. Examples: AMC Theatres, local independent cinema, drive-in movie theater. Distinct from MovieRentalStore, which is a business for renting movies.

types.embedding_query_text: Franchise: A media franchise consisting of related films, series, and other media. Also called universe, series, franchise. Examples: Marvel Cinematic Universe, MCU.

chosen_type.label: MovieSeries
chosen_type.justification: Marvel Cinematic Universe is a movie series/franchise, matching MovieSeries.

candidates.label: MovieSeries
candidates.comment: A MovieSeries, as a CreativeWorkSeries, is a collection of related movies. Also called film series, movie franchise, film saga. Examples: The Lord of the Rings trilogy, the James Bond film series, the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Distinct from MovieClip, which is a short segment of a single movie.

candidates.label: Series
candidates.comment: A general group of related items, which may or may not be of the same kind, forming a sequence or collection. Also called collection, sequence, set, installment. Examples: a book series, a lecture series, a product line, a collection of artworks. Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is a series of creative works.

candidates.label: VideoGameSeries
candidates.comment: A sequence of related video games, often sharing a common storyline, characters, or gameplay mechanics. Also called game franchise, video game saga, game series. Examples: The Final Fantasy series, The Elder Scrolls series, Grand Theft Auto series.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeries
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeries is an ordered collection of related published materials, such as books, periodicals, TV shows, or video games. Also called series, collection, franchise, saga. Examples: "Harry Potter" book series, "Star Wars" movie series, "The Simpsons" TV series, "The Legend of Zelda" video game series. Distinct from CreativeWorkSeason, which is a single installment within a series.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

types.embedding_query_text: Superhero: A fictional character with superhuman abilities who fights evil. Also called hero, crime fighter, superhuman. Examples: Ghost Rider.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: Ghost Rider is a fictional character, and Person includes fictional characters.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: ComicStory
candidates.comment: Any indivisible, re-printable unit within a comic, encompassing interior narratives, covers, and backmatter. Also called comic narrative, comic segment, comic content. Examples: The main story in a comic book, a short backup story, a comic book cover, an editorial page. Distinct from ComicCoverArt, which is specifically the artwork on the cover.

candidates.label: ComicIssue
candidates.comment: An individual, serially published installment of a comic series, uniquely identified by its series name, volume, issue number, and variant description. Also called comic book, comic installment, single issue comic. Examples: The Amazing Spider-Man #1, Detective Comics Vol. 2 #27, Saga #50, a one-shot comic. Distinct from ComicSeries, which is the overarching publication title.

candidates.label: ComicCoverArt
candidates.comment: The visual artwork specifically featured on the cover of a comic book or issue. Also called comic book cover, graphic novel cover, comic art. Examples: The cover of Action Comics #1, a variant cover for a Marvel comic, a graphic novel's front illustration. Distinct from ComicStory, which refers to any indivisible, re-printable unit of a comic, including interior stories.

candidates.label: Movie
candidates.comment: A creative work that is a motion picture film. Also called film, motion picture, cinema. Examples: "The Shawshank Redemption", "Avatar", "Parasite", "Casablanca". Distinct from TVSeries, which is a collection of episodes.

types.embedding_query_text: Company: A business organization that produces goods or services. Also called corporation, firm, studio. Examples: Marvel, Marvel Studios.

chosen_type.label: Corporation
chosen_type.justification: Marvel is a company, and Corporation is a specific type of company.

candidates.label: Corporation
candidates.comment: A Corporation is a legal entity separate from its owners, typically formed for business purposes. Also called company, incorporated business, limited company. Examples: Apple Inc., Google LLC, Microsoft Corporation, Coca-Cola Company. Distinct from Cooperative, which is an organization owned and operated by its members for their mutual benefit.

candidates.label: LocalBusiness
candidates.comment: A specific physical business or a branch of an organization that serves a local community. Also called local company, neighborhood business, regional enterprise. Examples: a local restaurant, a bank branch, a medical clinic, a bowling alley, a grocery store. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group of people with a particular purpose.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: Cooperative
candidates.comment: A Cooperative is an organization formed as a joint project by multiple organizations or individuals, often for mutual benefit. Also called member-owned business, co-op, collective. Examples: REI (Recreational Equipment, Inc.), Ocean Spray, Sunkist Growers, credit unions. Distinct from Corporation, which is a business entity owned by shareholders.

candidates.label: Consortium
candidates.comment: A membership organization typically composed of other organizations collaborating on a shared project or goal. Also called alliance, syndicate, federation, partnership. Examples: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), a research consortium, a banking consortium, a joint venture. Distinct from Organization, which is a general grouping of people or entities.

types.embedding_query_text: Convention: A large gathering of people with a common interest, often for entertainment. Also called conference, gathering, event. Examples: San Diego Comic-Con, comic book convention.

chosen_type.label: ConferenceEvent
chosen_type.justification: San Diego Comic-Con is a convention, and ConferenceEvent includes conventions.

candidates.label: ConferenceEvent
candidates.comment: An event specifically organized as a conference, typically involving presentations, discussions, and networking. Also called conference, convention, symposium, summit. Examples: A tech conference, an academic symposium, a business summit, a medical convention. Distinct from Event, which is a general occurrence.

candidates.label: SocialEvent
candidates.comment: An event primarily focused on social interaction and entertainment. Also called party, gathering, social function, get-together. Examples: a birthday party, a wedding reception, a community picnic, a networking mixer.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: ComedyEvent
candidates.comment: An event featuring comedic performances or content. Also called stand-up show, humor performance, comedy festival. Examples: A stand-up comedy show, a sketch comedy performance, a comedy festival, an improv night. Distinct from Event, which is a general occurrence.

candidates.label: LiteraryEvent
candidates.comment: An event focused on literature, such as readings, book launches, or discussions. Also called book event, author appearance, literary gathering. Examples: a poetry reading, a book signing, a literary festival, a panel discussion with authors.

types.embedding_query_text: Person: An individual human being. Also called individual, human, someone. Examples: Kevin Feige, Josh Horowitz, Shawn Levy, Feige.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: Kevin Feige, Josh Horowitz, and Shawn Levy are individual people.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: Audience
candidates.comment: An Audience is an Intangible entity representing the specific group of people for whom an item or creative work is intended. Also called target group, readership, viewership, demographic. Examples: children, teenagers, medical professionals, general public, investors.

candidates.label: IndividualPhysician
candidates.comment: An IndividualPhysician is a medical business representing a single medical practitioner. Also called doctor, medical doctor, general practitioner, specialist. Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

types.embedding_query_text: Film: A motion picture or movie. Also called movie, feature, picture. Examples: Star Wars: Starfighter, Starfighter.

chosen_type.label: Movie
chosen_type.justification: Star Wars: Starfighter is a film, and Movie is the direct type.

candidates.label: Movie
candidates.comment: A creative work that is a motion picture film. Also called film, motion picture, cinema. Examples: "The Shawshank Redemption", "Avatar", "Parasite", "Casablanca". Distinct from TVSeries, which is a collection of episodes.

candidates.label: MovieSeries
candidates.comment: A MovieSeries, as a CreativeWorkSeries, is a collection of related movies. Also called film series, movie franchise, film saga. Examples: The Lord of the Rings trilogy, the James Bond film series, the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Distinct from MovieClip, which is a short segment of a single movie.

candidates.label: MovieTheater
candidates.comment: A MovieTheater is a civic structure designed for public viewing of movies. Also called cinema, picture house, movie house. Examples: AMC Theatres, local independent cinema, drive-in movie theater. Distinct from MovieRentalStore, which is a business for renting movies.

candidates.label: ScreeningEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving the public showing of a movie or other video content. Also called film screening, movie showing, video presentation, cinema event. Examples: a film festival screening, a premiere showing of a new movie, a public documentary viewing, a drive-in movie night.

candidates.label: FilmAction
candidates.comment: FilmAction is a CreateAction representing the act of capturing sound and moving images on film, video, or digitally. Also called shooting a film, recording video, filming. Examples: Filming a movie scene, recording a documentary, shooting a wedding video, capturing a short clip on a phone.

types.embedding_query_text: Character: A fictional person or being in a story. Also called persona, role, figure. Examples: Carter Slade, Johnny Blaze, Blaze.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: Carter Slade and Johnny Blaze are fictional characters, and Person includes fictional characters.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: PerformanceRole
candidates.comment: A PerformanceRole, as a Role, is a role an entity plays in a theatrical performance, such as a movie or TV series. Also called acting role, character role, stage role. Examples: 'actor in a film', 'director of a play', 'musician in a concert'. Distinct from OrganizationRole, which is a role within an organization.

candidates.label: ProfilePage
candidates.comment: A ProfilePage is a WebPage dedicated to displaying information about a specific entity, such as a person or organization. Also called user profile, personal page, bio page. Examples: a LinkedIn profile, a social media user's page, an author's biography page, a company's "About Us" page.

candidates.label: ComicStory
candidates.comment: Any indivisible, re-printable unit within a comic, encompassing interior narratives, covers, and backmatter. Also called comic narrative, comic segment, comic content. Examples: The main story in a comic book, a short backup story, a comic book cover, an editorial page. Distinct from ComicCoverArt, which is specifically the artwork on the cover.

types.embedding_query_text: ComicBook: A publication containing sequential art and text, often featuring superheroes. Also called comic, graphic novel, issue. Examples: Marvel Spotlight issue 5, Marvel Spotlight.

chosen_type.label: ComicIssue
chosen_type.justification: Marvel Spotlight issue 5 is a single comic book issue, matching ComicIssue.

candidates.label: ComicSeries
candidates.comment: A sequential publication of comic stories released under a consistent unifying title. Also called comic book series, graphic novel series, comic strip series. Examples: The Walking Dead, Batman, X-Men, Calvin and Hobbes. Distinct from ComicIssue, which is a single installment within the series.

types.embedding_query_text: Deity: A god or supernatural being. Also called god, divine being, supernatural entity. Examples: Satan.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: Satan is a supernatural being, and Person includes fictional and mythological characters.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: HinduTemple
candidates.comment: A HinduTemple is a place of worship and civic structure dedicated to Hindu deities. Also called Mandir, Hindu shrine, temple. Examples: Akshardham Temple, Sri Venkateswara Temple, a local Hindu community temple.

candidates.label: MedicalEntity
candidates.comment: The most generic type of entity related to health and the practice of medicine. Also called healthcare entity, medical concept, health-related item. Examples: a disease, a drug, a doctor, a medical procedure, a hospital. Distinct from Thing, which is the root of all schema.org types.

candidates.label: Product
candidates.comment: A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering. Examples: a pair of shoes, a concert ticket, a car rental service, an episode of a TV show.

candidates.label: Church
candidates.comment: A civic structure serving as a place of worship for Christian congregations. Also called house of God, chapel, sanctuary, temple (Christian context). Examples: Westminster Abbey, a local Baptist church, a small village chapel. Distinct from PlaceOfWorship, which is a general term for any religious building.

types.embedding_query_text: Year: A period of 365 days (or 366 in a leap year) starting January 1. Also called calendar year, twelve months, annual period. Examples: 2028, 2026 edition, 1967, 1972.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.justification: Years like 2028, 1967, and 2007 are specific dates, and Date is the appropriate type.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

types.embedding_query_text: DayOfWeek: A day of the seven-day week, such as Sunday. Also called weekday, day, calendar day. Examples: Sunday.
